sources.title: Introduction: PID Controller Design
sources.author: University of Michigan Control Tutorials for MATLAB and Simulink
sources.content: A PID controller combines proportional, integral, and derivative action. Proportional action scales present error, integral action accumulates error over time, and derivative action responds to the rate of change of error. The three gains influence rise time, overshoot, settling time, steady-state error, and stability in different ways. Many practical designs use only a subset of the three terms.

sources.title: Introduction: System Analysis
sources.author: University of Michigan Control Tutorials for MATLAB and Simulink
sources.content: Closed-loop control measures system output, compares it with a reference, and uses the resulting error to determine the input. Time-domain response is commonly evaluated using rise time, overshoot, settling time, and steady-state error. Stability and model uncertainty must be considered when selecting controller gains.
